items.text: O ji ọsọ karịa ọsọ ìhè gbapụ, ma ọ bụghị, agaara m etikwasị ya ihe n'ike.
items.q: The speaker means he'd have hung him up by the backside. Is that clear?
before: …ka ọ gaara adị mgbe ahụ. Ka Farid na-agba ọsọ, ụkwụ ya zọrọ akwụkwọ Eskandar, dọwaa mkpuchi akwụkwọ ozi ya. Otu akụkụ nke aha ogologo akwụkwọ ahụ pụtara ìhè: "Puku Iri ... Ihe ịtụnanya, Ihe ọmụma ... Akụkọ ... Maka ..." Farid abịaghị n'ụlọ ahụ ụbọchị abalị abụọ ma ọ bụ atọ. Eskandar nọ na-asị:
– Ngwere obere ahụ mebikwara iwu physics.

items.text: Mmadụ na-amata mgbagwoju anya. Ka ị na-eche echiche banyere ya, mgbagwoju anya gị na-abawanye.
items.q: A student's crude slang for 'it makes your head spin' (like 'shit-dizzy'). Is there a crude word here? Which would a young person use?

items.text: Gị onwe gị, site n'ụdị olu amụ a ị na-eji ekwu okwu, aha gị kwesịrị ịbụ Alain Amụlon.
items.q: 'Alain Amụlon' is meant as a rude pun on the actor Alain Delon. Would Igbo readers get it? If not, what word could carry it?
before: – Ee, Hamoon bụ aha dị mma nye gị. Dịka Hamoon nke fim ahụ, gị onwe gị jupụtara n'ajụjụ. Ị jupụtara n'ụjọ, ị bụkwa isi iyi nke mgbagwoju anya, ọ bụghịkwa nye onwe gị, kama ọ bụ nye mụ onwe m.

items.text: Mmiri ozuzo anaghị esi n'ala na-ada rịgoro n'elu.
items.q: Her son says he would die for her; Maman objects. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Aka m dị mkpụmkpụ, mmekọrịta gị na m dịkwa anya.
items.q: Amir tells the girl he loves why he holds back. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Ana m ekwu na ọ bụrụ na ị na-anọdụ ebe a na-agụ uri mgbe niile, mmiri agaghị adị gị ọkụ.
items.q: A friend criticises Amir for reading poetry all day. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Bibi, Chukwu zoo mkpụrụ obi ya n'udo, na-ekwukarị n'oge dị otu a: ọ bụrụ na m ekwuo ya, ire m ga-ere ọkụ; ọ bụrụ na m ekwughị ya, ụmị ọkpụkpụ m ga-ere ọkụ.
items.q: Maman hesitates before criticising her husband. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: Ọ na-asị, "Afọ dị mma ka a na-amata site n'oge ifuru ya."
items.q: The family's New Year visits were cancelled; a brother jokes about it. An old Persian proverb kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?

items.text: – Enyi nwa nwanne nna anyị nwoke, onye nwe ọka aka nke ọgọ nwoke anyị, onye bụ ọgaranya kachasị na Tehran, gwara ya banyere ya.
items.q: Does it clearly say: the friend of the cousin of our in-law's master craftsman?
before: – Nyeghachi m ya. Dị ka a ga-asị na ọ maara otu ndị nwere waya na-arụ ọrụ.
Taghi jidere aka Hamid na ikuku zọpụta walkman ahụ. Ma Yaser nwetakwara ọtụtụ aka na ụkwụ. Hamid kwuru:

items.text: Dịka mgbe m bụ nwata, mgbe Maman na-atọpụ eri akwa uwe ochie, anyị na-eburu eriri ahụ gburugburu ụlọ ka eri akwa ahụ ghara ịkpọkọta n'elu ibe ya.
items.q: Is it clear the children walk around inside the house, holding the yarn?
before: …anya nke ihe omume ụwa ma a hapụ ide ha ede n'ebe a. E dere ha ka ha ghọọ àkwà mmiri n'agbata ụwa m na ụwa gị. Àkwà mmiri si n'ụwa m, n'oge m na-ede ahịrịokwu ndị a, gaa n'ụwa gị, n'oge ị ga-anọdụ ala ịgụ ha. Site n'akụkụ a, m na-atọpụ eriri okwu ahụ, gị onwe gị na-achịkọta ya site n'akụkụ nke ọzọ.
